correctness.rationale: The exact source-stage update yields the three-step companion with independent uniform coefficients. Recomputing the symmetric six-moment map gives T(X)=AXA^T+(z^4/12)X_33 e1e1^T. Cubic Jury conditions give the midpoint bound f(z)>0. The rank-one positive Lyapunov resolvent is H(z) as displayed, and 1-z^4 H(z)/12 factors as 4q(z)/[3(2-z)(z^2+2z+4)f(z)]. An explicit negative derivative makes q have one crossing in (0,delta). The positive definite dual eigenmatrix proves nondecay or growth for every nonzero deterministic starting state at/above the threshold before delta; Jensen proves failure beyond delta. A standalone self-contained exact-rational checker independently reconstructs the operator, Lyapunov identities and stage updates (239 checks). The finite tests do not replace the infinite proof.

value.rationale: The primary algorithm was proposed with finite-horizon accuracy analysis, leaving natural long-time memory-feedback stability unexplored. The exact algebraic cutoff solves a canonical scalar pure-delay test equation at the coarsest permissible lag-resolving grid, a conventional stability benchmark. It identifies an open interval (rho,delta) where mean and mean-square stability disagree, with an exact rational witness z=7/6; the exact boundary informs delay-step/stiffness selection and separates finite-horizon accuracy from infinite-horizon reliability. This structural transition and universal one-step stability classification are more substantive than a routine small-step sufficient bound or an arbitrary finite table. No multi-cell or nonlinear guarantees are claimed.
